title: Eight picks. Three cross-checks.
spoken: Eight sources, eight robot-vacuum winners. We checked the reviews behind them. These four picks reveal three useful patterns: a shared weakness, a result that doesn't generalize, and a clear head-to-head advantage. The other four stay open.
links: Eight-pick source matrix and supporting coverage

title: First cut: embedded pet hair
spoken: Pet hair embedded in carpet? RTINGS finds that both the Saros ten R and original Qrevo Curv struggle with it. So, for that priority, we'd set these two headline winners aside. Its dedicated pet-hair guide is the next stop, with alternatives tested specifically for that job.

title: The mopping result does not travel
spoken: Now the Curv two Flow—a different model from the original Curv. The Hook Up found it cleaned dried mud exceptionally well. Vacuum Wars found weak dried-stain cleaning, even with maximum water. Different protocols; the reason isn't established. We'd compare both tests before choosing the Flow for stubborn stains.

title: A comparison that does narrow the pair
spoken: Tall doorsteps give a clearer comparison. In The Hook Up’s same test, Curv two Flow failed a thirty-millimetre vertical face. The Dreame X sixty cleared fifty millimetres both ways. Between these two, we'd pursue the X sixty for tall thresholds. Watch the demonstration and compare your doorway's shape.
